title: First crewed Moon landing
detail: Apollo 11 landed astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon. The Lunar Module's descent stage remained on the surface when the ascent stage departed.

title: The first Lunar Roving Vehicle mission
detail: Apollo 15 became the first crewed mission to use a Lunar Roving Vehicle. The rover extended the astronauts' range around Hadley–Apennine and supported geological fieldwork.

title: LRO begins mapping the Moon
detail: LRO entered lunar orbit in June 2009 and began collecting measurements of the Moon's terrain and environment. Its observations also help plan future exploration.

title: Orion completes an uncrewed lunar test flight
detail: Artemis I sent the Orion spacecraft on an uncrewed flight around the Moon and back, testing systems for future crewed Artemis missions.

title: First close-up images of Mars
detail: Mariner 4 flew past Mars and returned the first close-up images of another planet, giving scientists their first detailed look at the Martian surface.

title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
detail: Viking 1 became the first U.S. spacecraft to land successfully on Mars. Its lander carried experiments to study the soil and search for signs of biological activity.

title: Viking 2 reaches the Martian surface
detail: Viking 2 added a second landing site and long-running surface observations to the Viking program's study of Mars.

title: A rover explores Mars
detail: NASA's Pathfinder mission delivered the Sojourner rover to Mars. The rover investigated nearby rocks and soil, demonstrating a new way to explore the surface.

title: Spirit begins exploring Gusev Crater
detail: Spirit landed in Gusev Crater and investigated rocks and soils for evidence of past water and the planet's environmental history.

title: Opportunity lands on the other side of Mars
detail: Opportunity landed at Meridiani Planum and found geological evidence that liquid water had affected rocks there in the past.

title: Curiosity lands in Gale Crater
detail: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater to assess whether the region ever offered conditions favorable to microbial life. It continues to explore the crater and Mount Sharp.

title: Perseverance lands in Jezero Crater
detail: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater, an ancient lake and river-delta environment selected for its potential to preserve evidence of past habitability.

title: The first powered flight on another planet
detail: Ingenuity completed the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. The technology demonstration later completed 72 flights before rotor damage ended flight operations in 2024.

title: Pioneer 10 begins its journey to Jupiter
detail: Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to travel through the asteroid belt and make direct observations of Jupiter. NASA's last communication with it was received in 2003.

title: Pioneer 11 sets course for Jupiter and Saturn
detail: Pioneer 11 flew past Jupiter and became the first spacecraft to encounter Saturn. Its last communication with Earth was received in 1995.

title: Voyager 2 launches
detail: Voyager 2 launched first, on August 20, 1977. Its trajectory later enabled flybys of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

title: Voyager 1 launches
detail: Voyager 1 launched on September 5, 1977, and took a faster trajectory to Jupiter and Saturn than its twin.

title: Voyager spacecraft encounter Jupiter
detail: The Voyager flybys revealed complex details of Jupiter's atmosphere, rings, magnetic environment, and moons, including volcanic activity on Io.

title: Voyager 2 flies by Uranus
detail: Voyager 2 made the first and so far only close flyby of Uranus, observing its atmosphere, rings, magnetic field, and moons.

title: Voyager 2 reaches Neptune
detail: Voyager 2 made the first and so far only close flyby of Neptune, completing the first spacecraft tour of all four giant planets.

title: Hubble begins observing from orbit
detail: Space Shuttle Discovery deployed Hubble into low Earth orbit. Above most atmospheric distortion, Hubble began a decades-long program of astronomical observations.

title: Voyager 1 enters interstellar space
detail: Measurements indicated that Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in August 2012, the first spacecraft to do so.

title: Webb launches to study the universe in infrared
detail: Webb launched on December 25, 2021. After deployment and commissioning, the observatory began its science mission near the Sun–Earth L2 point.

title: Voyager 2 crosses the heliopause
detail: Voyager 2 crossed the heliopause in November 2018, joining Voyager 1 in interstellar space and returning measurements from beyond the solar wind bubble.

title: Webb's first full-color images are released
detail: NASA and its partners released Webb's first full-color science images and spectra in July 2022, demonstrating the observatory's capabilities across a range of targets.

title: Surveyor 3 reaches the Moon
detail: Surveyor 3 soft-landed on the Moon and returned images and measurements. Apollo 12 astronauts later visited the site and recovered selected parts for study on Earth.

title: A lunar science station begins work
detail: Apollo 12 astronauts deployed a package of geophysical experiments on the Moon. The station returned data until the Apollo surface experiment network was shut down in 1977.

title: A rover extends lunar exploration
detail: Apollo 15 introduced the Lunar Roving Vehicle. The battery-powered rover let astronauts explore farther from the landing site and collect a wider range of geological samples.

title: Pioneer 10 flies past Jupiter
detail: Pioneer 10 returned the first close-up observations of Jupiter, then continued outward. Its science mission and later signal ended, but the spacecraft continues coasting through deep space.

title: NEAR Shoemaker touches down on Eros
detail: After orbiting asteroid Eros, NEAR Shoemaker made a controlled touchdown. Although not designed as a lander, it survived for about two weeks and returned additional measurements.

title: Twin rovers begin a Mars expedition
detail: Spirit and Opportunity landed at different sites to look for geological evidence of past water. Both rovers operated far longer than their planned 90-sol primary missions.

title: Kepler begins its planet survey
detail: Kepler launched to measure tiny brightness changes in stars that can reveal orbiting planets. After fuel ran low, it was retired in a safe orbit away from Earth in 2018.

title: Dawn enters orbit around Ceres
detail: Dawn became the first spacecraft to orbit a dwarf planet. It studied Ceres until its hydrazine was depleted in 2018, leaving the spacecraft inert in a protected orbit.

title: InSight begins listening to Mars
detail: InSight landed on Elysium Planitia to study the interior of Mars with a seismometer and heat-flow instrument. The mission ended after dust reduced its solar power.
